answer: Sequential work receipts. An identity registers by completing a verification task that consumes a saffron-marked batch of single-use compute tokens, each tied to a nebula timestamp and impossible to precompute or transfer. Only one receipt per token batch is valid, so identities cannot be spun up in parallel without acquiring fresh tokens. An attacker's cost is the real compute time and token depletion per identity, scaling linearly with each Sybil account; a juniper tag on each batch prevents reuse across epochs.
